waive.TypeOK: Shape check only: no behaviour change breaks it without also breaking a property below it.

mutations.name: unconfirmed-reservation-not-counted
mutations.why: An ambiguous write retains a reservation, but the capacity ledger ignores it and can admit another job.

mutations.name: retry-an-ambiguous-write
mutations.why: An ambiguous dispatch is put back in the queue even though the external write may already have taken effect.
mutations.search:
DispatchUnconfirmed(j) ==
    /\ j \in sent /\ j \notin launched
    /\ state[j] \in {"dispatching", "cancelling"}
    /\ state' = [state EXCEPT ![j] = "unconfirmed"]
mutations.replace:
DispatchUnconfirmed(j) ==
    /\ j \in sent /\ j \notin launched
    /\ state[j] \in {"dispatching", "cancelling"}
    /\ state' = [state EXCEPT ![j] = "held"]

mutations.name: recovery-forgets-durable-intent
mutations.why: Recovery treats an interrupted durable dispatch intent as a definite failure and releases its place.
mutations.search:
RecoverIntent(j) ==
    /\ j \in sent
    /\ state[j] \in {"dispatching", "cancelling"}
    /\ (state[j] = "dispatching" \/ j \notin launched)
    /\ state' = [state EXCEPT ![j] = "unconfirmed"]
mutations.replace:
RecoverIntent(j) ==
    /\ j \in sent
    /\ state[j] \in {"dispatching", "cancelling"}
    /\ (state[j] = "dispatching" \/ j \notin launched)
    /\ state' = [state EXCEPT ![j] = "failed"]

mutations.name: reuse-raw-completion
mutations.why: A raw completion enters the green cache before the final judge has accepted fresh matching facts.
mutations.search: IF j \in Outside THEN "gone" ELSE facts

mutations.name: reuse-stale-wrong-sha-or-blocked
mutations.why: The final judge can mark stale, wrong-SHA, or release-blocked facts green.

mutations.name: count-own-jobs-only
mutations.why: Admission counts only the places its own jobs hold: a person's run, another repo's or another program's heavy command already fills the pool and the hub admits on top of it.

mutations.name: count-from-the-poll-only
mutations.why: Admission reads the pool's running count from the poller's snapshot instead of its own ledger: a job it dispatched that GitHub does not list yet is not counted, and the next pump admits another into the same place.

mutations.name: free-the-place-at-the-cancel
mutations.why: A superseded run's place is given back when the hub asks GitHub to cancel it, not when GitHub shows it ended: the next job is admitted while the cancelled one still runs.

mutations.name: ignore-the-account-limit
mutations.why: Admission checks the job's own pool and not the account's limit on all hosted jobs: Linux jobs fill the account while macOS jobs run.

mutations.name: no-account-hold
mutations.why: The design's first rule (F1 before the owner's decision): a release entry waiting on macOS holds no account place, so a land job behind it takes the account's last place, an outside Linux job takes the place the ending macOS run frees, and the release job finds macOS free and the account full.

mutations.name: hold-counts-for-entries-ahead
mutations.why: Every held place counts against every waiting job, those ahead of the holder included: a release Linux entry that waited first is kept out of the account's free place by the hold of a release macOS entry behind it.

mutations.name: requeue-a-failed-dispatch
mutations.why: A dispatch that failed or timed out puts its entry back in the queue: it is admitted and dispatched a second time, although the first dispatch may have started the run.

mutations.name: order-ignores-the-lane
mutations.why: The pump takes the oldest entry whatever its lane: a branch job that arrived first takes the free place a release job waits for.

mutations.name: order-ignores-the-arrival
mutations.why: The pump orders by lane only: of two branch jobs the later one takes the free place the earlier one waits for.

mutations.name: supersede-a-release-run
mutations.why: The supersede rule forgets the release lane: a newer run of the same repo, ref and workflow cancels a release run.

mutations.name: supersede-a-merge-queue-run
mutations.why: The supersede rule forgets the merge queue's lane: a newer run of the same repo, ref and workflow cancels a queue run.

mutations.name: supersede-a-run-the-hub-does-not-govern
mutations.why: The supersede rule cancels every older run GitHub lists for the key, a person's among them.

mutations.name: supersede-another-key
mutations.why: The supersede rule does not compare repo, ref and workflow: a start cancels a run of another ref.

mutations.name: supersede-before-the-pause-check
mutations.why: A start cancels the older runs of its key before it finds admission paused: the old run is cancelled and nothing replaces it.
mutations.search: out == IF decision = "held" THEN Superseded(j) ELSE {}
mutations.replace: out == IF decision # "reused" THEN Superseded(j) ELSE {}

mutations.name: supersede-on-a-reused-answer
mutations.why: A start that is answered from a green run, and so starts no run of its own, still cancels the older runs of its key.
mutations.search: out == IF decision = "held" THEN Superseded(j) ELSE {}
mutations.replace: out == IF decision # "refused" THEN Superseded(j) ELSE {}

mutations.name: reuse-any-finished-run
mutations.why: Reuse looks for a finished run of the digest, not a green one: a start is answered `reused` from a red run.

mutations.name: reuse-by-ref-not-digest
mutations.why: Reuse is keyed on the repo, ref and workflow instead of the input digest: a start is answered from a green run of other inputs.

mutations.name: pump-ignores-the-pause
mutations.why: Pause refuses new starts but the pump keeps admitting what already waits: a job starts while the owner paused admission.

mutations.name: start-ignores-the-pause
mutations.why: `start` does not read the owner's pause: a start made while paused is queued instead of refused.
mutations.search: decision == IF paused THEN "refused" ELSE IF
mutations.replace: decision == IF FALSE THEN "refused" ELSE IF

mutations.name: admit-a-lapsed-entry
mutations.why: The pump does not read the lease: it starts the job of a session that died while it waited.

mutations.name: late-heartbeat-renews-the-lease
mutations.why: The heartbeat handler sets a new deadline without reading the old one: an entry whose lease lapsed, and that others were admitted past, is live again.

mutations.name: a-lapsed-entry-blocks-the-queue
mutations.why: The pump's order counts every held entry, lapsed ones too: a dead session's entry at the head keeps a live one from a free place until the sweep removes it.
mutations.search: \E r \in Jobs : Waiting(r) /\ Competes(r, j) /\ Ahead(r, j) /\ Room(r)
mutations.replace: \E r \in Jobs : state[r] = "held" /\ Competes(r, j) /\ Ahead(r, j) /\ Room(r)

mutations.name: strict-head-of-line
mutations.why: The pump waits for the first entry in line even when that entry cannot start: a release macOS job that waits for a macOS runner keeps every Linux job out of the account places it does not hold.

mutations.name: no-lease-sweep
mutations.why: Nothing removes an entry whose lease lapsed: a dead session's entry stays in the queue for good.

mutations.name: pump-not-run-when-a-place-frees
mutations.why: Nothing runs the pump when a place frees (a run ends and no start arrives): the release job that waits is never admitted.

mutations.name: a-failed-dispatch-keeps-its-place
mutations.why: A dispatch that failed never gives its place back: the pool stays full of entries that run nothing and the release job waits for good.

mutations.name: a-dispatch-failing-after-a-supersede-keeps-its-place
mutations.why: A newer start supersedes an entry while its dispatch is awaited (cancelling); the dispatch then fails, and only an entry still dispatching is ended: no run of it exists to be seen ending, so its place is never given back and the release job behind it waits for good.
